chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed by me while I was sitting with a judge in Medina. I visited him the next day, and he asked me, 'What was the session in which I saw you yesterday?' I said, 'May I be your ransom, this judge is very generous to me, and perhaps I sat with him.' He said, 'What guarantees you that the curse will not descend and encompass everyone in the session?'
ai.seo_question: What is the risk of sitting with a judge according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) cautions a companion against assuming the piety of a judge merely due to his generosity, warning that divine curse may encompass the entire gathering if the judge is not truly righteous. This highlights the Shia scholarly principle of *al-wala' wa al-barra'* (affiliation and disaffiliation), emphasizing that social association with authority figures carries spiritual risk if their inner state is unknown. The warning serves as a reminder to maintain discernment in religious and social circles, ensuring one's standing is not inadvertently affected by the status of those around them.
